# Antigravity Interface Contract

<!-- GENERATED from src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/antigravity.contract.ts by scripts/generate-contract-docs.mjs — do not edit. Run `npm run contract:docs`. -->

Every external interface of Antigravity that Cinna relies on, one entry each: what the tool must do, which Cinna code depends on it, and what the user loses when it stops. **Verified against Antigravity ACP server 1.4.5** — the version pinned in `src/shared/runtimePins.ts`.

Each entry has exactly one test, titled with its id, in [`antigravity.contract.test.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/antigravity.contract.test.ts). They run the real pinned binary over stdio against a loopback fake provider — no login, no provider request — with `npm run test:contract` (`make contract ENGINE=antigravity` installs the binary first). They are not part of `npm test`.

The raw shapes a run observes are compared with the committed [`antigravity-1.4.5.json`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/snapshots/antigravity-1.4.5.json), and a difference fails the run; `make contract-snapshot ENGINE=antigravity` rewrites it once a change is understood. To evaluate a new release, `make contract-next ENGINE=antigravity VERSION=<x.y.z>` runs the same tests against that version without changing the pin; red entries name their owners below, and the run prints the diff between the pinned snapshot and the candidate's (written to a temp path, never into the tree) — that diff is what changed.

Hand-written evidence and reasoning stay in [The ACP Engine Contract](../acp_contract.md); this file is only the index of what is checked.

**Flow step** names the step of the Level 2 whole flow that exercises the entry — **A** plain chat on the Default runtime, then its title (the engine’s own on Codex, Cinna’s AI title elsewhere); **B** a specialist @-added mid-chat, called through Cinna’s MCP server; **C** continuity: a later turn remembers the first; **D** a specialist attached before the first turn. A dash means no step does, and the note says why. No Level 2 variant walks them for Antigravity yet: neither the no-billing `e2e/specs/runtime-flow.spec.ts` nor `make live-flow` runs it. The fake provider here is the server’s own `gateway` auth mode, so no Google login is involved.

## Launch & env

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `antigravity.launch.version-flag` | CLI: `--version` | Exits 0 and prints the binary’s build information, one line of which is `Build label: <version>`. Cinna never runs it: the resolver treats the server as versionless and the pinned sha256 is the only proof of version. | [`binaryResolver.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/binaryResolver.ts) `ANTIGRAVITY_SPEC`<br>[`binaryResolver.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/binaryResolver.ts) `versionless` | Nothing today. If the flag became fatal, a resolver that started probing it would discard every install; if the label stopped matching the pin, the managed copy is not the version the contract describes. | — no Level 2 whole flow runs Antigravity yet |
| `antigravity.launch.server-args` | CLI: `--uid=` | On macOS the server starts with no arguments, and `--uid=` is fatal: `Unknown command line flag 'uid'`, non-zero exit. (Linux takes `--uid=` per the ACP registry; the contract has only run on macOS.) | [`antigravityEnv.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityEnv.ts) `antigravityServerArgs` | Every Antigravity session fails to start on the platform whose arguments are wrong. | — no Level 2 whole flow runs Antigravity yet |
| `antigravity.launch.gemini-home` | env var: `GEMINI_HOME` | The server reads `antigravity-acp/settings.json` from, and keeps its conversations and MCP tool schemas under, the home this variable names; unset, the home is `$HOME/.gemini`. | [`antigravityLauncher.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityLauncher.ts) `antigravityIsolatedHome`<br>[`antigravityLauncher.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityLauncher.ts) `prepareAntigravityHome`<br>[`antigravityEnv.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityEnv.ts) `antigravityHome` | A sealed folder would run on the user’s own `~/.gemini` — its skills and MCP servers — or lose its conversations between processes, so a chat could not be resumed. | — no Level 2 whole flow runs Antigravity yet |
| `antigravity.launch.command-cwd` | file: `Command Working Directory` | The system instruction names the session’s cwd as its `Command Working Directory`, both when `GEMINI_HOME` is nested inside that cwd and when the home is outside it (a native folder on `~/.gemini`). 1.3.0 named `<home>/antigravity-cli/skills` in the second case; pinned both ways, so a release that brings that back fails here. | [`antigravityLauncher.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityLauncher.ts) `antigravityIsolatedHome` | A sealed folder’s commands and relative paths would run in the engine’s skills directory; a native folder depends on the prompt naming the folder as long as the second half holds. | — no Level 2 whole flow runs Antigravity yet |

## Limits

| `antigravity.limits.quota-exhausted` | ACP field: `agent_message_chunk "Usage Limit Reached"` | A model request answered 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` with a `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` of reason `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` and `quotaResetDelay` in its metadata ends the turn with one `agent_message_chunk` `"Usage Limit Reached\n\nYou have reached your current quota for this period. Your limit will reset in <N units>[, <M units>]."` and then `stopReason: "end_turn"` — no error, no `_meta`, and no `usage` when the turn used no tokens. When the quota runs out on a later model call, the notice follows the turn’s earlier tool calls as its last update. | [`antigravityLauncher.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityLauncher.ts) `ANTIGRAVITY_QUOTA_HEADER`<br>[`antigravityLauncher.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityLauncher.ts) `ANTIGRAVITY_QUOTA_BODY`<br>[`antigravityLauncher.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/antigravityLauncher.ts) `antigravityQuotaNotice`<br>[`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `engineTurnEndError` | A user out of Antigravity quota sees the notice as the agent’s answer to their message — a turn that looks finished, with no error — or, if the wording changes, the turn reads as an ordinary reply again. | — no Level 2 whole flow runs Antigravity yet |
